text:
alyssa: Heads up — I hit a weird perf and correctness combo on an internal LLM flow with Mistral 8x7B. Sliding-window + max_position_embeddings tweak caused mask "snapback" on long streams

toni: ugh what do you mean by snapback?

alyssa: When we force max_pos=2048 for client X, after ~1500 tokens the attention mask seems to shift and the kernel chooser flips to generic matmul mid-request, latency spikes ~3x. Not a pure correctness drop but outputs repeat phrases.

kevin: can you paste the config you used?

alyssa: config snippet:
```
model_config: {
  name: "mistral-8x7b",
  max_position_embeddings: 2048,
  rope_scale: 1.0,
  head_kv_dim: 128
}
runtime: {
  kernel_policy: ["pref_fused_attn", "fallback_generic"],
  batching: { auto_slice: true, slice_ms: 12 }
}
```

samir: interesting. so kernel chooser switched -> fallback_generic? any perf logs?

alyssa: yes, nvprof and our tracer show a kernel switch event at token ~1532. Before that avg token p95 ~18ms, after jump to ~62ms. Also saw KV cache writes increase 2.5x.

benchbot: perf-report: throughput=46 toks/s @ 1k, 14 toks/s @ 1.6k. kernel=fallback_generic after 1.53k.

toni: hypothesis: rope wrapping + sliding window boundary crosses a block that invalidates our fused-attn strides so we hit an unimplemented path. Maybe the fused kernel assumes contiguous offsets inside a single max_pos chunk.

kevin: we saw something similar on Mixtral run last month — kernel chooser uses sequence-length buckets and also checks (seq_len + kv_cache_offset) % tile_size == 0. If offset jumps due to sliding window prefetching, it doesn't match and forces generic path.

alyssa: yep that matches. Also noticed our batching heuristic merged a request that had a non-zero kv_offset with one fresh request. The merged batch had heterogeneous offsets -> chooser opted safe generic.

samir: quick mitigation: change batching.auto_slice to false for this client and force per-request kernel_hint=pref_fused_attn?

alyssa: tried kernel_hint, helped latency but caused slight quality regressions in very long flows (we lost some cache hits since we disabled safe fallback). Still better than 3x spike.

kevin: long-term fix: make chooser shard-aware and accept heterogeneous kv_offsets by computing per-sample stride metadata. Also we should add a lightweight fast-path check that allows fused kernel when all samples have same tile alignment OR when padding can be introduced cheaply.

toni: agreed. I'll open a perf/chooser PR. Also we need a unit test that simulates sliding-window wrap at various window sizes + max_pos overrides.

alyssa: logged a small repro harness: run ./bench/repro_long_window.sh --model mistral-8x7b --maxpos 2048 --window 1024 --batch 2

kevin: can you attach the nvprof snippet? even a tail of the log helps.

alyssa: pasted short excerpt:
```
[1531] kernel_choice: pref_fused_attn
[1532] kernel_choice: fallback_generic  // attendance_stride_mismatch
[1532] gpustats: kernel_time 62.4ms, memcopy 9.2ms
[1533] kv_write_ops:+1.8x
```

samir: I want to understand the KV thrash — is it reserializing caches when alignment changes?

alyssa: looks like we rebase cached KV buffers to a new base index and copy into new tiles instead of view-slicing. That copy kills perf.

benchbot: note: adding a copy avoidance path reduces p95 by ~28% in our bench.

toni: action items:
- [toni] PR: chooser tolerance for tile misalignment w/ opt-in flag (perf/chooser)
- [kevin] bench: add harness variants for mixed kv_offset batches, report p50/p95 and kernel path counts
- [samir] runtime: add cheap check to avoid deep-copy when kv rebase is monotonic shift
- [alyssa] doc: add that clients should avoid batching requests with different kv_offset for now (temporary)

kevin: also add a regression monitor in console that counts kernel path switches per model-version. If a build starts hitting generic path >X%, alert.

alyssa: +1 — created a minimal alert query: kernel_path:count_over_time(model:mistral-8x7b, path==fallback_generic, 5m) > 5

samir: merging these should address both perf and shallow correctness. We should also try rope_scale tweaks as a short test — scaling down to 0.98 reduced boundary jitter in earlier experiments.

alyssa: tested rope_scale=0.98 locally — the switch moved to ~1.7k tokens (better) but still happened. So it's a partial mitigation.

kevin: good to capture in changelog. anyone want to pick up the PRs?

toni: I'll take chooser PR today.

samir: I'll do runtime copy-avoidance tomorrow.

alyssa: I'll update docs + add repro to infra. Thanks team. :rocket:

deploy-bot: deploy queued for branch perf/chooser-tolerance at 1981024000 (staging)

alyssa: will run the bench on staging once deployed and post results here.
